- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to model output.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment changes sharply downward (e.g., -0.5 to -1.0) and news volume is low, model may lag; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to reflect sentiment shift.
- When sentiment is flat (≤0.33) and news volume is high, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to capture momentum.
- Model tends to overcorrect after mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 3–5 consecutive days of price decline); reduce forecast by 0.5–2% to avoid premature reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment is rising (positive change) and news volume is rising, model may be too optimistic; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to reflect caution.
